guide.title: Muradin's Overview
guide.text:
Muradin is a generalist Tank that excels at disrupting
the enemy team, dealing damage, and surviving kill attempts. His versatile kit allows
him to do many things, from peeling to diving,
from scouting to ganking.
During the laning phase, he can focus on giving vision as well as messing up
enemy rotations by dismounting and chunking down enemy Heroes.
Dwarf Toss allows him to easily escape from most situations.
Second Wind denies all damage he received. Meanwhile,
he farms stack for his Baseline Quest
which empowers Storm Bolt.
During team fights, he can either play defensively or offensively.
The choice depends on the situation, your team composition, and the enemy team composition.
When playing defensively, he mainly focuses on peeling and/or
counter-engaging for his team.
When playing offensively, he primarily focuses on engaging
and/or diving vulnerable enemy Heroes.

guide.title: Muradin's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Strong self-sustain
Decent crowd control
Good mobility
Weaknesses
Not able to peel from high mobility Heroes (like Tracer)
Weak to crowd control that can stop Dwarf Toss

Muradin's Dwarf Toss Build is quite versatile as it is designed to increase
your damage output, your survivability, and your utility when necessary.
When played properly, it can create a lot of space and be very impactful in team fights.
Bronzebeard Rage at Level 13 is a key Talent in this Build
as it allows you to deal a lot of damage while also healing yourself in the process.
Note that it requires you to have good aim with Storm Bolt.
If the opponents do not have any Hero with fast-hitting Basic Attacks
but they have at least one Hero with slow but heavy-hitting Basic Attacks,
you should pick Dwarf Block at Level 1 to be more durable.
If your team lacks sustain healing or does not have a Healer

guide.title: Muradin's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Muradin synergizes with
Being able to follow up on Muradin's Storm Bolt
with a devastating burst damage combo is what makes Mages
(for example Li-Ming) his ideal partners.
Chaining crowd control Abilities one after another
is so valuable in this game that having another Hero who can provide this kind of effects
from another Role (such as Blaze played as Offlaner)
in your team will make Muradin a real threat for the enemy team.
Muradin is countered by
Heroes who can deal percent-based damage (such as
Tychus via Minigun) can shred Muradin's Health
very quickly, especially while in Avatar.
When played quick enough, crowd control Abilities
(for example Face Melt by E.T.C.) puts a lot of pressure
on him because they can stop Dwarf Toss, his only form of escape.

guide.title: Muradin's Maps
guide.text:
Muradin's stronger maps
Muradin's average maps
Muradin's weaker maps
In the hand of experienced players,
Muradin is good on Maps where he can use his innate resilience
and mobility to harass enemy Heroes
and enable plays for his entire team by aggressively but safely invading
the enemy side of the Map during the early game
(such as Hanamura Temple).
On the other hand, he is bad on Maps where the Objective takes a long period of time
(for example Braxis Holdout) because he will eventually run out of Mana,
effectively denying his Trait value.

guide.title: Muradin's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Storm Bolt should be used with patience and combined with the Slow provided by Thunder Clap when possible.
Thunder Clap is a decent peeling tool, especially against melee Heroes who rely on Basic Attacks.
Dwarf Toss allows you to disengage when low Health, but be careful when the enemy Heroes have crowd control.
Avatar is a maximum Health boost that protects you from burst damage but makes you vulnerable to percent-based damage.
Haymaker should mostly be used for peeling away enemy Heroes rather than to engage by pushing enemy Heroes towards your team.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Muradin's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Muradin is a well-rounded Tank that can provide vision,
engage, and peeling to his team.
Thanks to Dwarf Toss allowing him to quickly escape when in danger,
Muradin can easily scout the enemy side of the battlefield to give his team a vision advantage,
but only if the enemy team does not have tools to easily stop Dwarf Toss
during its animation.
During team fights, Storm Bolt and Thunder Clap
are decent crowd control tools that can be used to
either engage enemy Heroes or peel for allied Heroes.

abilities.title: Muradin's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
Storm Bolt should be used with patience and combined with the Slow provided by Thunder Clap when possible.
Thunder Clap is a decent peeling tool, especially against melee Heroes who rely on Basic Attacks.
Dwarf Toss allows you to disengage when low Health, but be careful when the enemy Heroes have crowd control.
Avatar is a maximum Health boost that protects you from burst damage but makes you vulnerable to percent-based damage.
Haymaker should mostly be used for peeling away enemy Heroes rather than to engage by pushing enemy Heroes towards your team.

abilities.title: Storm Bolt
abilities.text:
Storm Bolt
(Q)
Muradin
Mana: 45
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Throw a hammer, dealing 110 (+4% per level) damage to the first enemy hit and Stunning them for 1.25 seconds
Quest: Basic Attack Heroes affected by Stuns, Slows, or Roots. Slowed or Rooted enemies grant 1 stack. Stunned enemies provide 2 stacks. If the Hero dies within 3 seconds, gain 5 stacks.
Reward: Upon hitting 45 targets, Storm Bolt pierces to hit an additional target, and Muradin's Basic Attacks reduce the cooldown of Storm Bolt by 0.5 seconds and restore 3 Mana.
Mythic Reward: Upon hitting 160 targets, Storm Bolt's range is increased by 50%, width increased by 100%, and now pierces all targets.
Storm Bolt is a Basic Ability which provides Muradin
a ranged Stun. As a Muradin player, you should take
your time to closely watch how enemy Heroes are moving because this Ability
has a small delay and the projectile is not that fast, making it hard to connect
if you do not predict the target's movement, assuming they are trying to
juke you. Generally speaking, you should avoid using
Storm Bolt on high-mobility
Heroes if there are other good targets to use it on because there is a high
chance you will miss them and thus waste an important cooldown.

abilities.title: Thunder Clap
abilities.text:
Thunder Clap
(W)
Muradin
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 8 seconds
Blast nearby enemies for 96 (+4% per level) damage and Slow them by 30% for 2.5 seconds. Heroes hit also have their Attack Speed reduced by 30% for the duration.
Thunder Clap is a Basic Ability that
Slows, reduces the Attack Speed, and deals damage
to every enemy in a small radius around Muradin. You can use this Ability
to lower the chances to miss Storm Bolt
thanks to the Slow provided and/or to reduce the damage done by enemy Heroes
who heavily rely on Basic Attacks do deal damage.

abilities.title: Dwarf Toss
abilities.text:
Dwarf Toss
(E)
Muradin
Mana: 55
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Leap to target location, dealing 59 (+4% per level) damage to enemies on landing. Upon leaping, gain 30 Armor for 2 seconds, reducing damage taken by 30%.
Dwarf Toss is a Basic Ability that allows Muradin
to quickly change position, to either reach enemy Heroes or run away from them.
Whether to use it aggressively or defensively depends on the situation.
When you are in danger, use it to escape or to gain Armor
(for example when Kael'thas uses Pyroblast on you).
A good trick to suddenly reach safety is to leap over impassable terrain,
especially useful when trying to escape from enemy Heroes who do not have such tool.
When your team is in danger, use it to peel.
While it does not provide any peeling on its own, it allows you quickly
reposition near allied Heroes who need help.
When your team wants to force a team fight, use it to engage. While it slightly
increases your survivability by giving you Armor, be extremely
careful when choosing to do so because you will not have your escape anymore.
Before doing aggressive plays like this, always check the Minimap to see
if your team is close enough to follow you immediately, else you will end up
dying alone for no reason, and make sure your team is ready to
follow-up for securing a kill.

abilities.title: Avatar
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Avatar
(R)
Muradin
Heroic
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 90 seconds
Transform for 20 seconds, gaining 1000 Health.
Avatar is a Heroic Ability that increases Muradin's
maximum Health for 20 seconds. The additional Health he immediately receive
acts as a form of burst healing that helps him to survive
when being focused by the enemy team.
The exact moment when to use it depends on how you expect the fight to go. Do not use it too early,
else the enemy team will just disengage and wait for it to expire. Do not use it too late,
else the enemy team will crowd control you to death
before you will be able to cast it.

abilities.title: Haymaker
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Haymaker
(R)
Muradin
Heroic
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 40 seconds
Stun target enemy Hero, and wind up a punch dealing 319 (+4% per level) damage and knocking the target back, hitting enemies in the way for 319 (+4% per level) damage and knocking them aside.
Haymaker is a Heroic Ability that should usually be used to
push dangerous enemy Heroes far from your team as a form of peeling
or as an interrupt for dangerous Abilities,
however, it can occasionally be used to push vulnerable enemy Heroes
towards your team as a form of engage.

abilities.title: Second Wind
abilities.text:
Second Wind
(D)
Muradin
Passive
Muradin restores 55 (+4% per level) Health per second when he has not taken damage for 4 seconds. When below 40% Health, increased to 111 (+4% per level) Health per second.
Second Wind is a Trait that allows Muradin to
quickly regenerate his Health when not taking damage. Experienced players will get
a lot of value out of it by constantly harassing enemy Heroes during the
early game, while scouting
and stopping rotations, and during team fights,
by getting out for a few seconds while extremely low on Health
only to heal up and go in again when at medium/high Health.
The ability to passively heal yourself between fights allows you to stay on the
battlefield for long periods of time. That said, while you will never need to use your
Hearthstone to regenerate your Health, your Mana will eventually reach critical
values and force you away from the battlefield for a while.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text:
Muradin has a Baseline Quest which requires to hit enemy Heroes
with Basic Attacks while they are affected by a Stun,
Root, or Slow. You also get 5 stacks when
an enemy Hero dies within 3 seconds of being hit by Storm Bolt.
Upon reaching 45 stacks, Storm Bolt can pierce the first target hit
and Muradin's Basic Attacks restore 3 Mana and reduce the cooldown of Storm Bolt by 0.5 seconds.
Upon reaching 160 stacks, you unlock the Mythic Reward: Storm Bolt's range is increased by 50%
and width is increased by 100%, and pierces all targets.
The first Reward allows you to Stun 2 enemy Heroes if they happen
to be lined up, to cast Storm Bolt more often if you have
an enemy to hit with Basic Attacks and the enemy team has no Blinds,
or simply to Stun an enemy Hero who is hiding behind
another enemy (usually a Minion, Summon, or Monster). Last but not the least,
you can also use Basic Attacks on any enemy to restore a small amount of Mana.
If you use Storm Bolt while far away from your target, you
will only be able to get 2 stacks per cast. If you use Storm Bolt
while your target is within range of your Basic Attacks and your Basic Attacks are not
on cooldown, you will have enough time to hit them with 2 Basic Attacks while they are
Stunned and therefore gain 4 stacks per cast. While it will not
always be possible to cast Storm Bolt in melee range,
it is good to be aware of this interaction.
The best way to get stacks on your own is to roam on the battlefield
and find isolated enemy Heroes to harass them with Thunder Clap,
Storm Bolt, and Basic Attacks. You generally want to keep
Dwarf Toss off cooldown and only use it to escape, ideally
over impassable terrain because a lot of Heroes cannot follow you over it.
The best way to get stacks with the help of your team is to have an allied Hero
with a Stun to use as follow-up
to Storm Bolt (for example Tyrande
with Lunar Flare). Since the target will be
Stunned for longer, you will get double stacks per
Basic Attacks for longer. When doing so, make sure to wait for their
cooldown to be back before using Storm Bolt again.

Skullcracker at Level 7 can be situationally picked
as an interrupt against enemy Heroes who rely on
channeled Abilities (notably Yrel).

Muradin's Thunder Clap Build is designed to increase your survivability
at the cost of damage output, in order to survive against team compositions
that can take down any target, regardless of how much maximum Health they have.
Compared to other Builds, you will have more self-healing
in team fights because of Healing Static
at Level 13 combined with Thunder Burn at Level 4.

you should pick Dwarf Block at Level 1 to be more durable.

at all, you should consider picking Third Wind at Level 1.

for Storm Bolt when going for aggressive plays whereas

as an interrupt against enemy Heroes who rely on
channeled Abilities (notably Yrel).

Muradin's Storm Bolt Build is quite versatile as it is designed to increase
your damage output, your survivability, and your utility when necessary.
When played properly, it can create a lot of space and be very impactful in team fights.

talent_pages.title: Level 1 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
?
Dwarf Block
(Level 1)
Muradin
Casting Dwarf Toss grants 3 charges of Block. Each Block charge grants 75 Physical Armor against a single enemy Hero Basic Attack, reducing the damage taken by 75%.
Dwarf Block is a situational Talent that gives
Physical Armor in the form of
Block charges
immediately after casting Dwarf Toss.
When you are in a safe area and you do not expect to be in danger for a dozen of seconds,
you can Dwarf Toss just to get 3 Block stacks
from this Talent because they do not expire over time. Always do this once
before the game stars, and every time you use your Hearthstone. You can
occasionally also do it while on the battlefield, but only when you are safe
and you will not need to use Dwarf Toss soon.
Block charges are especially valuable
when facing Heroes with slow but heavy-hitting Basic Attacks (such as Hanzo) and
terrible when playing against Heroes with fast-hitting Basic Attacks (D.Va,
Genji, Kharazim, Lúcio, Tassadar, Tracer,
and Tychus). Heroes with Clones (for example Nova) can consume them faster
too, however, it is generally not a problem because their AI will not always target you.
?
Third Wind
(Level 1)
Muradin
Increases Health Restoration rate to 90 (+4% per level) per second, and raises Health threshold to 60% Health for improved 180 (+4% per level) per second Restoration.
Third Wind is a good Talent that allows Muradin
to get an even more favorable trade when damaging enemy Heroes
and getting damaged in return because he will get his Health back for free
by staying far from the action for a dozen of seconds, a strategy that is
extremely valuable on his best Maps (for example Battlefield of Eternity).
✔
Give 'em the Axe!
(Level 1)
Muradin
Attacking a Hero that is Stunned, Rooted, or Slowed increases Muradin's Basic Attack damage by 40% for 3 seconds.
Give 'em the Axe! is a good Talent that increases the damage
done by your Basic Attack for a few seconds when hitting enemy Heroes who are
Stunned, Rooted, or Slowed.
This effect allows Muradin to pressure enemy Heroes on his own.
Even though allied Heroes with access to the required
crowd control effects can help with it,
Muradin can trigger this Talent on his own
by relying on the following Abilities and Talents:
Storm Bolt;
Thunder Clap;
Thunder Burn at Level 4;
Imposing Presence at Level 16.

talent_pages.title: Level 4 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
?
Sledgehammer
(Level 4)
Muradin
Storm Bolt deals 500% damage to non-Heroic enemies. Stormbolt cooldown is reduced by 1.5 seconds.
Sledgehammer is a situational Talent that slightly
reduces Storm Bolt's cooldown and heavily increases
the damage done by Storm Bolt when used
against non-Heroic enemies. This includes Minions, Mercenaries,
Monsters, and Summons.
We find this Talent to be a nice tool for clearing Mercenary Camps featuring
exactly 2 Mercenaries (for example, Siege Giants on Cursed Hollow) because,
after unlocking Storm Bolt's pierce from
Muradin's Baseline Quest,
you can easily hit both of them at the same time with it. If someone else in your team
is taking care of Mercenary Camps, you do not need to pick this Talent for that.
The best Maps for this Talent are:
Battlefield of Eternity (for Immortal)
Cursed Hollow (for Siege Camp);
Blackheart's Bay (for Siege Camp and Doubloon Camp);
Dragon Shire (for Siege Camp);
Garden of Terror (for Siege Camp);
Sky Temple (for Siege Camp).
✔
Reverberation
(Level 4)
Muradin
Increases the Attack Speed Slow of Thunder Clap from 30% to 50% and the duration from 2.5 seconds to 3.5 seconds. Each enemy Hero hit reduces your Heroic Ability cooldown by 5%.
Reverberation is a good Talent that empowers
Thunder Clap against Heroes who rely on Basic Attacks
and reduces the cooldown of your Heroic Ability by a small amount—by
4.5 seconds when playing Avatar and by 2 seconds
when playing Haymaker.
The cooldown reduction provided by this Talent may be occasionally useful on Battlegrounds
where there is more frequent action, usually because the Objective is constantly active
or tends to spawn again within 70-80 seconds, which is slightly lower than
Avatar's cooldown.
When having this Talent, if you are fighting and your Heroic Ability is still on cooldown
for a dozen of seconds or less, keep an eye on it because it may become available
and make the difference between losing or winning the battle!
?
Thunder Burn
(Level 4)
Muradin
Hitting an enemy Hero with Thunder Clap triggers a second Thunder Clap explosion 2 seconds later in the same location that deals 72 (+4% per level) damage.
Thunder Burn is a good Talent that makes
Thunder Clap explode a second time, for a portion of its damage, 2 seconds after
hitting an enemy Hero with the first explosion.
The second explosion heals yourself as much as the
first explosion if you have Healing Static at Level 13
or deals 75% damage of the first explosion to isolated enemy Heroes
if you have Thunder Strike at Level 13.
Remember that it is possible that the enemy Heroes dodge the first explosion,
unless you use Storm Bolt to keep them there.

talent_pages.title: Level 7 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
?
Perfect Storm
(Level 7)
Muradin
Storm Bolt's cooldown is reset and 25 Mana is refunded if an enemy dies within 3 seconds of being hit by it. This effect has an 8.5 second cooldown.
Perfect Storm is a decent Talent that resets
Storm Bolt's cooldown and restores 25 Mana whenever an enemy dies
within 3 seconds of being hit by it. This effect has a 8.5-second cooldown.
This effect can be triggered by killing non-Heroes too,
however, that is only useful after unlocking Storm Bolt's piece
from Muradin's Baseline Quest.
When fighting enemy Heroes near non-Heroes,
try to aim Storm Bolt so that it hits an enemy Hero
and a non-Hero at the same time. If the non-Hero dies but the Hero does not die,
you will be able to cast a second Storm Bolt on that Hero.
If you pick Sledgehammer at Level 4, it will be more likely
that non-Heroes hit by Storm Bolt will die within 3 seconds,
increasing the likelihood that Storm Bolt's cooldown will be reset.
This synergy is particularly good when playing against Heroes who can spawn Summons (such as
Anub'arak and Zagara) and/or when playing on Battlegrounds that feature
Monsters with low maximum Health (notably Guardians on Infernal Shrines).
?
Heavy Impact
(Level 7)
Muradin
Enemies hit by Dwarf Toss are Slowed by 80% for 1.5 seconds.
Heavy Impact is a good Talent that makes
Dwarf Toss apply a huge
Slow effect to all enemies hit when landing.
You can use the Slow provided to peel
for your team, to increases the chance that Storm Bolt will hit,
to get a good angle for Haymaker by walking around
the enemy Hero you intend to hit, or for body-blocking.
✔
Skullcracker
(Level 7)
Muradin
Every 3rd Basic Attack against the same enemy deals 90% bonus damage and Stuns them for 0.25 seconds.
Skullcracker is a good Talent that causes every
third Basic Attack to hit harder and briefly Stun the target.
The bonus damage also works on non-Heroes, even though they do not get Stunned.
You can use Skullcracker's brief Stun
as an interrupt. For doing so,
you have to hold your third Basic Attack until you will need
its Stun effect. While this is the correct way to use
Skullcracker as an interrupt,
note that it makes you lose damage and not get the cooldown
reduction for Storm Bolt.
The best Heroes to use Skullcracker against are:
Anduin, to interrupt Holy Word: Salvation if picked;
Azmodan, to interrupt All Shall Burn;
Cassia, to interrupt Fend
or to make her lose Armor from Avoidance;
Chen, to interrupt Fortifying Brew;
Dehaka, to interrupt Drag or Brushstalker;
D.Va, to interrupt Defense Matrix;
Fenix, to interrupt Warp;
Gul'dan, to interrupt Drain Life if W Build;
Sonya, to interrupt Whirlwind;
Yrel, to interrupt her Basic Abilities when cast without using Divine Purpose.
You can also use its short Stun
as a setup for your own Storm Bolt
against enemy Heroes who have a way to dodge it
but can be easily hit with Basic Attacks. This is generally not needed because
Thunder Clap is usually enough for that.

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
✔
Avatar
(Level 10)
Muradin
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 90 seconds
Transform for 20 seconds, gaining 1000 Health.
Avatar is a strong Heroic Ability that heavily boosts
Muradin's survivability by increasing his maximum Health, therefore it has synergy with
percent-based healing effects and suffers percent-based damage.
In case you picked it, remember to use Stoneform during Avatar
to increase its effectiveness from 30% to around 40% of Muradin's baseline maximum Health.
Sometimes you will have to wait a bit for their cooldowns to be aligned again.
?
Haymaker
(Level 10)
Muradin
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 40 seconds
Stun target enemy Hero, and wind up a punch dealing 319 (+4% per level) damage and knocking the target back, hitting enemies in the way for 319 (+4% per level) damage and knocking them aside.
Haymaker is a situational Heroic Ability that
should mostly be used to push a dangerous enemy Hero away from your team and
fight with a numerical advantage for a few seconds.
Do not pick this Talent when
the enemy team can easily kill you because Avatar
will help you against team compositions that want to focus you.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
✔
Bronzebeard Rage
(Level 13)
Muradin
Deal 15 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies and heal for 75% of the damage dealt. Hitting an enemy Hero with Storm Bolt increase this damage by 200% for 3 seconds.
Bronzebeard Rage is a strong Talent that provides
a small amount of area of effect damage and self-healing,
increased for a few seconds after hitting enemy Heroes with Storm Bolt.
If you wish to make this Talent more reliable, you can combine it with either
Heavy Impact or Skullcracker
at Level 7 because they help you connect Storm Bolt.
?
Healing Static
(Level 13)
Muradin
Muradin heals for 6% of his maximum Health for each Hero hit by Thunder Clap.
Healing Static is a good Talent that provides self-healing
to Muradin when hitting enemy Heroes with Thunder Clap,
especially if he is surrounded by multiple enemy Heroes.
The second explosion of Thunder Clap generated by
Thunder Burn at Level 4 also benefits from this Talent,
so it can deal more damage to isolated enemy Heroes. Remember that the second
explosion will not happen if you do not hit at least one Hero with the first one.
?
Thunder Strike
(Level 13)
Muradin
Thunder Clap deals 200% more damage if only one target is hit.
Passive: Increase the duration of Dwarf Toss's Armor by 2 seconds.
Thunder Strike is a decent Talent that drastically
increases the damage done by Thunder Clap if it hits
a single enemy, regardless of it being a Hero or not. Furthermore, it makes the
Armor you receive from Dwarf Toss
last longer.
The second explosion of Thunder Clap generated by
Thunder Burn at Level 4 also
benefits from this Talent. Remember that the second explosion will not go off
if you do not hit a Hero with the first explosion
and that the bonus damage will not happen if another enemy enters the area.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
✔
Dwarf Launch
(Level 16)
Muradin
Increase the range of Dwarf Toss by 30%. Hitting an enemy Hero with Dwarf Toss reduces its cooldown by 1 second.
Dwarf Launch is a strong Talent that heavily
increases the distance covered by Dwarf Toss, allowing
Muradin to engage from a high distance,
and slightly reducing the cooldown of Dwarf Toss
when hitting enemy Heroes with it.
The small cooldown reduction provided by this Talent
slightly helps you mitigate the fact you are wasting your only form of escape to engage,
however, this bonus is so low that will not be enough to allow a quick retreat right after jumping aggressively
but you will have to stay there for multiple seconds before having Dwarf Toss available again.
?
Stoneform
(Level 16)
Muradin
Activate to heal Muradin for 30% of his maximum Health over 10 seconds. Second Wind is disabled during this time.
Stoneform is a good Talent that increases
Muradin's survivability by a solid amount, especially if you chose
Avatar at Level 10.
Considering it has a long cooldown, do not waste it out of combat and
make sure to have it available before engaging the enemy team.
Ideally, you want
to activate it during Avatar in order
to regenerate a larger amount of Health per second.
?
Imposing Presence
(Level 16)
Muradin
Cooldown: 20 seconds
Activate to reduce the Attack Speed by 50% and Movement Speed by 20% of nearby Heroes and Summons for 2.5 seconds.
Passive: Heroes and Summons that attack your Hero have their Attack Speed Slowed by 20% for 2.5 seconds.
Imposing Presence is a situational Talent that passively
reduces the Attack Speed of enemy Heroes attacking Muradin and, when activated,
applies a Slow and reduces the Attack Speed of nearby enemy Heroes and Summons.
We find this Talent useful when facing Heroes with Summons
(for example Raynor with Raynor's Raider at Level 10),
when playing against Heroes with high Attack Speed
(such as Tracer), or when the enemy team features Heroes with Basic Attacks
that can hit multiple times (so D.Va, Genji, and Lúcio).
Attack Speed reduction effects stack additively but a Hero's total Attack Speed
cannot be reduced below 25% of their base Attack Speed. Because of this,
you should wait 2.5 seconds before using Thunder Clap
on enemy Heroes affected by Imposing Presence, and vice versa.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Muradin
talent_pages.text:
?
Unstoppable Force
(Level 20)
Muradin
While active, Avatar grants 20 Armor and causes Muradin's Basic Attacks to reduce the cooldowns of Thunder Clap and Dwarf Toss by 0.75 seconds.
Unstoppable Force is a decent Talent that increases
Muradin's survivability by giving him some Armor and allows
him to reduce the cooldown of Thunder Clap
and Dwarf Toss with each Basic Attack.
?
Grand Slam
(Level 20)
Muradin
Haymaker gains a 2nd charge and its damage is increased by 25%. If a Hero dies within 3 seconds of being hit by Haymaker, instantly gain 1 charge.
Grand Slam is a decent Talent that adds a second
charge of Haymaker
and makes them deal 25% more damage. Furthermore, takedowns on enemy Heroes recently hit
by Haymaker restore 1 charge.
✔
Mountain King
(Level 20)
Muradin
Thunder Clap and Dwarf Toss each gain a 2nd charge.
Mountain King is a strong Talent that passively gives
a second charge of Thunder Clap
and Dwarf Toss for you to use when needed.
The second charge of Thunder Clap is not that useful on its own
but can be great when having Reverberation at Level 4
for more peeling against Heroes who rely on Basic Attacks,
Healing Static at Level 13 for self-healing,
or Thunder Strike at Level 13 for dealing
more burst damage. When trying to mitigate damage
from Basic Attacks, avoid casting Thunder Clap
twice in quick succession (within 2.5 seconds, or within 3.5 seconds
if you have Reverberation at Level 4) because
that will cause the Attack Speed reduction effect to overlap.
The second charge of Dwarf Toss allows you to have
an escape after using the first charge to engage.
When really needed, you can also use both charges for running away.
If you have Dwarf Block at Level 1, you will be
able to gain more Block charges while fighting.
If you have Heavy Impact at Level 7, you will be
able to use Slow enemy Heroes more often in team fights,
or to Slow them and still have a charge to get out.
If you have Dwarf Launch at Level 16,
it will be easier for you to reposition offensively or defensively.
?
Hardened Shield
(Level 20)
Muradin
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Activate to gain 75 Armor for 4 seconds, taking 75% less damage.
Hardened Shield is a situational Talent that may be useful when
you struggle to survive during team fights in the late game because
the enemy team is just focusing you with burst damage
and/or because they have too many ways to interrupt
Dwarf Toss mid-animation.
Pick this Talent when the enemy team can easily kill you,
and already did a handful of times during the game.
When you feel in danger, we suggest you to activate it as soon as possible,
before you get denied by crowd control.
